units.text: INT. COUNTY COURTHOUSE - COURTROOM 3 - NIGHT
The room after everyone has gone.
Folding chairs askew, a fan turning lazily above empty benches, a bailiff's coffee cup still ringing the oak rail.
The jury box is a row of pressed-flat cushions.
RHEA KOSTOPOULOS, 40s, defense attorney, sits alone at the long table with her shoes off and her jacket over the chair.
The verdict form lies in front of her.
She has read it twelve times.
The side door opens.
WALTER NGATA, 50s, prosecutor, tie loosened to half-mast, carries two paper cups and sets one on her table without a word.
He lowers himself into the chair opposite, and for a while the only sound is the fan, the clock, the hum of the vending machine in the corridor.
She lifts the cup, sniffs it, takes a sip, and winces.
He does the same and winces in precisely the same way, and they both look at the cups as if the coffee had betrayed them both equally.
It's terrible.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: It's honest.
units.name: RHEA

units.text: I wanted to say good trial.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: You won, Walter. You can say anything.
units.name: RHEA

units.text: I know. That's why it's hard to say.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: She turns the verdict form face down.
He watches her do it.
Then he stands, crosses to the jury box, and picks up a cushion that has slid off a seat, patting it back into place as though it matters.
She laughs once, without humor, and he turns.
What?
units.name: WALTER

units.text: You're tidying.
units.name: RHEA

units.text: Habit.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: Thirty years and you still fix the chairs.
units.name: RHEA

units.text: Someone has to.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: Hector Salas is going away for twenty-five years.
units.name: RHEA

units.text: He was guilty.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: He was nineteen.
units.name: RHEA

units.text: So was the boy in the road.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: Silence.
The fan ticks.
She looks at her hands.
I know. I stood there while his mother cried, and I thought, I'm on the wrong side of this room.
units.name: RHEA

units.text: You weren't.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: No. I wasn't. Somebody had to be.
units.name: RHEA

units.text: He sits again, heavily.
Pushes the cup toward the center of the table.
She pushes hers to meet it.
Want to get a drink?
units.name: WALTER

units.text: I want to go home and sleep for a week.
units.name: RHEA

units.text: That's a no.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: That's a ask me again in a month.
units.name: RHEA

units.text: I will.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: She stands, gathers her files and her shoes, the verdict form folded into her briefcase.
At the door she pauses with a hand on the light switch.
Walter.
units.name: RHEA

units.text: Yes?
units.name: WALTER

units.text: Fix the chairs on your way out.
units.name: RHEA

units.text: She flicks the switch.
Half the room goes dark.
He sits a moment longer in the remaining light, then rises and begins, one by one, to straighten them.
